findings.evidence: erasure: delete or anonymise in live systems, propagate to processors and derived data (search indexes, caches, analytics, ML features)
findings.explanation: The procedure authorizes an agent to perform irreversible deletion across many systems without an explicit human approval or checkpoint. A mistaken or fraudulent erasure request could cause widespread data loss. Add a mandatory approval step by the DPO/operator before executing destructive actions and clearly limit scope.

findings.evidence: Respond in clear language through a secure channel
findings.explanation: Sending the response or personal data export externally is an external message/transfer; the skill does not require explicit approval of the recipient and channel before dispatch. Add a confirmation step and verified destination.

findings.evidence: delete or anonymise in live systems, propagate to processors and derived data (search indexes, caches, analytics, ML features)
findings.explanation: Erasure obligations for ML features/models and derived data are context-dependent; deleting or retraining them may not be required or feasible and can cause collateral damage. Require a legal/technical assessment per system.

findings.evidence: Classify the right: ... portability (20), objection (21)
findings.explanation: Article 20 portability applies only to personal data provided by the data subject, processed by automated means, and based on consent or contract; the skill does not state these conditions, so an agent may over-export. Add the Art. 20 criteria.

findings.evidence: legal retention (for example accounting records)
findings.explanation: Retention periods such as accounting-records obligations vary by jurisdiction and document type; the example may be wrong in some countries. Tell the reader to verify the applicable retention schedule.
